title: Finite generic flatification after a birational base modification
statement: Let $S$ be an integral quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], where quasi-compact quasi-separated means that it has a finite affine open cover with quasi-compact pairwise intersections. Let $f:X\to S$ be dominant and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; dominant means that its image is dense. Write $K=k(S)$ and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-sc-generic-point]. There exist an integral scheme $S_1$, a proper surjective morphism $b:S_1\to S$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism] whose generic fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}K$, and a finite morphism $a:X_1\to X\times_S S_1$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-pc-base-change] such that $a_\eta$ is an isomorphism, there is an open $U_1\subset X\times_S S_1$ whose inclusion and inverse-image inclusion are schematically dense [def-trf-schematically-dense-open] and over which $a$ is an isomorphism, and $X_1\to S_1$ is flat and finitely presented [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The generic fibre is schematically dense in $X_1$, meaning that sections of $\mathcal O_{X_1}$ on any open are determined by their restrictions to its generic fibre.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, Step 0, printed pp. 21–22; Raynaud–Gruson, Théorème 5.2.2, as cited there. The target-side schematically dense eta-isomorphism open is retained as required by the sourced eta-modification conclusion.
